Revised assessment incorporating economic-finance literature:
The statement is a classic flexible inflation-targeting stance: with inflation still above target and labor markets tight, “ongoing increases” and a “sufficiently restrictive” stance align with Taylor-rule prescriptions and historical evidence that credible anti-inflation policy reduces inflation at some near-term output cost (Taylor; Romer and Romer; Sargent, The Conquest of American Inflation). The explicit recognition of cumulative tightening and transmission lags reflects optimal policy tradeoffs emphasized in model-based analyses (Wieland; Svensson and Woodford). Implementation via a higher interest on reserve balances (4.65%) leverages the post-2008 floor system to transmit policy efficiently (Board of Governors; interest on reserves). Continued balance-sheet runoff (Treasuries and agency MBS) constitutes quantitative tightening that can raise term premia and tighten financial conditions via expectations channels documented in asset-pricing and term-structure research (Cochrane and Piazzesi; QE/QT transmission literature). Forward-looking, data-dependent guidance aims to anchor inflation expectations—central in inflation forecast targeting frameworks.

Net tone: hawkish but measured. The acknowledgement that “inflation has eased somewhat” softens the message, yet the commitment to further tightening and QT keeps the balance slightly negative for near-term growth-risk sentiment.
